title: Because Of: Causes on the Pacific Coast

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6: formal ways to say "because of" and "as a result of". They link a cause to a consequence and are followed by a noun, never by a verb. The Pacific coast of Colombia is full of such links: the rain, the forest and the rivers explain how people live and travel.

sections.title: Cause and consequence
rows: Debido a la lluvia y a la selva, hay pocas carreteras.
*debido a* + noun (*la lluvia*, *la selva*); the consequence follows
Debido al mal tiempo, las lanchas no salieron.
A raíz del terremoto de 1979, el tsunami destruyó muchas casas en Tumaco.
*a raíz de* + *el* becomes *a raíz del*; it often introduces an event
Los ríos son importantes porque llueve mucho.
with a verb (*llueve*) use *porque*, not *debido a*

items.spanish: Debido a la lluvia y a la selva, hay pocas carreteras en el Pacífico.
items.english: Because of the rain and the forest, there are few roads on the Pacific coast.

items.spanish: Debido a las lluvias, los ríos son los caminos de la región.
items.english: Because of the rains, the rivers are the roads of the region.

items.spanish: A raíz del terremoto de 1979, el tsunami destruyó muchas casas en Tumaco.
items.english: As a result of the 1979 earthquake, the tsunami destroyed many houses in Tumaco.

items.spanish: Debido al mal tiempo, las lanchas no salieron.
items.english: Because of the bad weather, the boats did not leave.

sections.content: *Debido a* and *a raíz de* take a noun: *debido a la lluvia*. If you want a verb, change the connector: *porque llueve mucho*. *A raíz de* fits best when the cause is an event that changed things (*a raíz del terremoto*).
